headline: Understand what consumers really mean.
subtitle: Identify hidden bias in consumer surveys, improve question wording, and collect insights your team can confidently act on.

painPoint.title: Small wording choices can create expensive conclusions.
painPoint.description: When surveys unintentionally guide participants toward an answer, apparent consumer demand may not reflect real buying behavior.

items.title: Inflated interest
items.description: Leading questions can make consumers appear more enthusiastic than they really are.

items.title: Unreliable segmentation
items.description: Biased responses can distort the preferences attributed to different customer groups.

items.title: Risky decisions
items.description: Teams may invest in campaigns or products based on signals their questions helped create.

solution.title: Turn consumer feedback into clearer evidence.
solution.description: CogBias reviews survey wording before launch so your team can distinguish genuine consumer sentiment from question-driven noise.

steps.title: Detect
steps.description: Find leading language, framing effects, social desirability pressure, and other cognitive biases.

steps.title: Improve
steps.description: Receive neutral alternatives that preserve your research goal without steering the participant.

steps.title: Decide
steps.description: Use more dependable consumer evidence to guide positioning, segmentation, and strategy.

outcomes: More reliable concept and message testing

cta.title: Consumer insight starts with better questions.
cta.description: Review your survey questions with CogBias before they reach your consumers.

headline: Build a stronger survey.
subtitle: Get clear guidance on cognitive bias and question wording before collecting data for your class project, thesis, or dissertation.

painPoint.title: Your results are only as reliable as the questions behind them.
painPoint.description: Even a well-designed study can be weakened by questions that lead participants, combine multiple ideas, or encourage socially desirable answers.

items.title: Hidden bias
items.description: Survey bias can be difficult to recognize when you are deeply familiar with your topic.

items.title: Unclear questions
items.description: Loaded, ambiguous, or double-barreled wording can make responses difficult to interpret.

items.title: Limited feedback
items.description: Students may not receive detailed survey feedback until late in the research process.

solution.eyebrow: A research assistant for your questions
solution.title: Improve your instrument before data collection begins.
solution.description: CogBias helps you understand what may be influencing a question and gives you actionable ways to improve it.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Analyze each survey question for cognitive bias and common wording problems.

steps.title: Learn
steps.description: See explanations that help you understand why a particular question may affect responses.

steps.title: Revise
steps.description: Compare suggested alternatives and select the wording that best supports your research objective.

outcomes: A clearer and more defensible survey instrument
Fewer avoidable issues during faculty review

cta.title: Give your research a stronger foundation.
cta.description: Find and improve potentially biased survey questions before collecting your data.

headline: Protect research quality
subtitle: Systematically identify cognitive bias in survey instruments and create clearer questions for rigorous, reproducible research.

painPoint.title: Instrument bias can quietly influence an entire study.
painPoint.description: Subtle framing and wording effects can alter participant responses, complicate interpretation, and weaken the validity of otherwise rigorous work.

items.title: Researcher assumptions
items.description: Domain expertise can make unintended assumptions in question wording harder to notice.

items.title: Inconsistent review
items.description: Manual instrument review may vary across researchers, labs, and projects.

items.title: Downstream consequences
items.description: Question-level problems may surface only after recruitment and data collection are complete.

solution.title: Add a consistent bias check to your methodology.
solution.description: CogBias supports researchers with structured detection, contextual explanations, and revision recommendations.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: Evaluate questions against a structured knowledge base of cognitive biases and survey-design risks.

steps.title: Validate
steps.description: Review bias classifications, explanations, and potential effects in the context of your research goal.

steps.title: Document
steps.description: Use improved wording and consistent review practices across researchers, instruments, and studies.

outcomes: Reduced risk of preventable response bias

cta.title: Bring structured bias detection into your research workflow.
cta.description: Improve survey questions without losing the intent of your study.

headline: Ask without leading.
subtitle: Design research questions that uncover how users actually think, behave, and experience your product.

painPoint.title: Users often tell us what our questions invite them to say.
painPoint.description: When a team is invested in a design, assumptions can enter interview prompts and surveys without anyone noticing.

items.title: Confirmation bias
items.description: Questions may search for support for an existing design instead of testing it openly.

items.title: Positive framing
items.description: Product language can encourage participants to evaluate an experience more favorably.

items.title: Polite responses
items.description: Participants may soften criticism when questions create social pressure or signal a preferred answer.

solution.title: Make space for honest user feedback.
solution.description: CogBias helps UX teams uncover leading language and rephrase questions while preserving the learning objective.

steps.title: Detect assumptions
steps.description: Find language that presupposes success, satisfaction, usefulness, or a particular user behavior.

steps.title: Rephrase neutrally
steps.description: Turn validation-focused prompts into open questions that welcome positive and negative feedback.

steps.title: Share better evidence
steps.description: Bring stakeholders findings that more accurately represent the user experience.

cta.title: Let users tell you what you did not expect.
cta.description: Use CogBias to create more neutral UX research questions.

headline: Validate the opportunity.
subtitle: Improve discovery questions before biased feedback turns into roadmap commitments, wasted development, or false confidence.

painPoint.title: A convincing survey result is not always a reliable product signal.
painPoint.description: Teams can unintentionally frame questions around the solution they want to build, producing evidence that appears to validate an existing idea.

items.title: False validation
items.description: Leading questions can transform tentative interest into what looks like strong product demand.

items.title: Roadmap risk
items.description: Biased evidence can move low-value ideas ahead of more meaningful customer problems.

items.title: Expensive rework
items.description: Weak discovery may not become visible until after design and engineering resources are committed.

solution.title: Pressure-test the question before trusting the answer.
solution.description: CogBias helps product teams separate customer evidence from the assumptions embedded in their research.

steps.title: Find bias
steps.description: Identify questions that assume a problem, promote a solution, or exaggerate purchase intent.

steps.title: Preserve the goal
steps.description: Rephrase questions without losing the product decision or hypothesis your team needs to investigate.

steps.title: Prioritize confidently
steps.description: Use clearer evidence when evaluating opportunities and making roadmap decisions.

cta.title: Build from customer evidence—not question bias.
cta.description: Improve your discovery questions before they influence your roadmap.

headline: Separate buyer intent
subtitle: Ask discovery questions that uncover genuine customer needs without creating artificial agreement, urgency, or purchase intent.

painPoint.title: A positive conversation does not always mean purchase intent.
painPoint.description: Customers may agree with persuasive framing, answer politely, or respond to the seller’s enthusiasm without revealing what they will actually buy.

items.title: Artificial agreement
items.description: Leading questions can make prospects appear more aligned with the proposed solution.

items.title: Overstated intent
items.description: Hypothetical enthusiasm may be mistaken for urgency, budget, or willingness to purchase.

items.title: Weak qualification
items.description: Teams may prioritize accounts using intent signals their own questions helped produce.

solution.title: Keep the commercial goal. Improve the signal.
solution.description: CogBias helps sales teams recognize when persuasion is distorting discovery and suggests questions that reveal authentic buyer priorities.

steps.title: Detect influence
steps.description: Find leading, loaded, assumptive, and socially pressuring language in discovery questions.

steps.title: Rephrase
steps.description: Preserve sales context while giving the buyer space to disagree, deprioritize, or identify a different need.

steps.title: Qualify accurately
steps.description: Base follow-up, forecasting, and account prioritization on clearer buyer evidence.

cta.title: Discover what buyers need—not what they will agree to.
cta.description: Use CogBias to improve the questions behind your sales decisions.
